title: East Africa Planting Calendar — Bimodal Rainfall Zones
content:
## East Africa Planting Calendars — Bimodal Rainfall Zones

Most of Kenya, Tanzania (highlands), and Uganda receive two rainy seasons per year.

### Long Rains Season (Masika)

**Rains arrive:** March (Coast/lowland) — April (Highlands)
**Plant:** 2–3 weeks after first good rains, when soil is moist 10cm deep
**Main crops:** Maize, beans, sorghum, vegetables
**Harvest:** July–September

| Crop | Plant date (highlands) | Plant date (lowland) | Harvest |
|------|----------------------|--------------------|---------|
| Maize (early) | 1–15 March | 15 Feb – 1 March | June–July |
| Maize (medium) | 15 March – 15 April | 1–15 March | July–August |
| Beans | 1 March – 15 April | 15 Feb – 1 March | May–June |
| Tomatoes (transplant) | 1–15 March | 15 Feb – 1 March | May–July |
| Kale/Sukuma | March–April | Feb–March | May onwards |

### Short Rains Season (Vuli)

**Rains arrive:** October (Coast) — November (Highlands)
**Plant:** October–November
**Main crops:** Maize, beans, vegetables
**Harvest:** January–March

| Crop | Plant date | Harvest |
|------|-----------|--------|
| Maize | Oct 15 – Nov 15 | Jan–Feb |
| Beans | Oct 15 – Nov 30 | Dec–Jan |
| Tomatoes | Oct 15 – Nov 15 | Jan–Mar |

### Special Notes by Zone

**Kenya Central (Kirinyaga, Nyeri, Murang'a):**
- March–May long rains; October–December short rains
- Coffee flowering: March–April; harvest: Oct–December
- Tea: year-round harvest; peak: April–June and October–December

**Kenya Rift Valley (Nakuru, Eldoret, Uasin Gishu):**
- March–May long rains (most reliable)
- Short rains erratic — do not rely for maize
- Wheat: plant June–July (cool season); harvest Nov–Dec

**Tanzania Northern (Arusha, Kilimanjaro, Moshi):**
- Long rains: March–May
- Short rains: November–January (Vuli)
- Coffee/banana year-round with irrigation
- Tomato: best transplant October for Nov–Jan harvest (short rains), or with borehole irrigation any month avoiding peak late-blight humidity

**Uganda (Kampala, Mbale, Mbarara):**
- First rains: March–May
- Second rains: August–November
- Maize planted in both seasons
- Banana: year-round production

### Key Rule: Plant Within 2 Weeks of First Good Rains

For rain-fed crops, delayed planting by 3+ weeks reduces yields 20–40%. The soil must have moisture 10–15cm deep before planting. Do not plant dry — germination will fail.

## Kalenda ya Upanzi Afrika Mashariki

### Masika (Mvua Ndefu)

Mvua inafika: Machi (pwani) — Aprili (milima)
Panda: wiki 2–3 baada ya mvua ya kwanza nzuri
Vizao: Mahindi, maharagwe, mboga
Vuvio: Julai–Septemba

### Vuli (Mvua Fupi)

Mvua inafika: Oktoba (pwani) — Novemba (milima)
Panda: Oktoba–Novemba
Vuvio: Januari–Machi

### Kanuni Muhimu

Panda ndani ya wiki 2 baada ya mvua ya kwanza nzuri. Kuchelewa wiki 3+ kunapunguza mavuno 20–40%.

title: Commercial Tomato Schedule — Arusha with Borehole Irrigation
content:
## Full Tomato Planting-to-Harvest Schedule (Arusha, Irrigated)

With borehole irrigation you are not locked to rain alone, but disease pressure and market timing still matter.

### Recommended first-season calendar (Northern Tanzania)

| Week | Stage | Activities |
|------|-------|------------|
| −6 to −4 | Land prep | Plough, lime if needed, manure, form raised beds, lay drip lines |
| −4 to −3 | Nursery | Sow hybrid seed in trays/beds; keep moist; protect from heavy rain |
| −1 | Harden | Reduce water slightly; expose seedlings to outdoor sun 3–5 days |
| 0 | Transplant | Evening transplant; water in; stake or trellis indeterminate types |
| 1–3 | Establish | Gap-fill; weed; start CAN top-dress week 3–4 |
| 4–6 | Vegetative | Stake/prune; scout daily for wilt and pests; mulch |
| 6–8 | Flowering | Shift to P/K emphasis; maintain even soil moisture (prevent blossom-end rot) |
| 8–14 | Harvest | Pick every 2–3 days at breaker/pink stage for transport; peak lasts 4–8 weeks |

**Days to first harvest:** 75–100 days from transplant for common East African hybrids (Anna F1, Kilele F1, Tylka F1).

### Best transplant windows near Arusha

1. **October–November** — targets Nov–Jan / early market; cooler nights; watch late blight if rains are heavy
2. **February–March** — targets May–July shortage prices if you can irrigate through dry spells
3. Avoid starting a large block that matures in the worst glut weeks when every neighbour harvests at once — **stagger 2–3 plantings** 14–21 days apart

### Variety × schedule tips

- **Anna F1 / Kilele F1:** Prefer for Arusha commercial fresh market; stake well
- **Roma VF / Cal J:** More determinate; shorter harvest window — good for processing contracts
- With irrigation, you can plant almost any month, but **high humidity + cool nights** (peak Masika) raise late blight risk — intensify fungicide scouting then

### 2-acre labour sketch

- Nursery: 3–5 person-days
- Transplant: 8–12 person-days
- Peak harvest weeks: 2–4 people daily for picking and grading

## Ratiba ya Nyanya za Biashara — Arusha kwa Umwagiliaji wa Kisima

### Kalenda fupi

| Wiki | Hatua |
|------|-------|
| −6 hadi −4 | Andaa shamba, chokaa, samadi, drip |
| −4 hadi −3 | Kitalu — panda mbegu |
| 0 | Pandikiza jioni; nyunyiza maji |
| 1–3 | Gusa pengo; lima magugu; anza CAN |
| 6–8 | Maua — weka unyevu sawa |
| 8–14 | Vuna kila siku 2–3 |

**Siku hadi mavuno ya kwanza:** 75–100 baada ya kupandikiza (Anna F1, Kilele F1, Tylka F1).

### Dirisha bora Arusha

1. Oktoba–Novemba
2. Februari–Machi (kwa bei Mei–Julai)

Panda kwa hatua kila siku 14–21 ili kuepuka kuuza yote wakati wa wingi.
